title: Policy translation, dual-write observability, and customer rollforward guidelines for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Deliver an operational playbook and automation for migrating customers from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 that minimizes user-visible change and preserves audit fidelity. Scope includes policy translation rules, dual-write behavior and safety nets, backfill reconciliation, SSO/SAML role mapping verification, observability hooks for canaries, and standardized customer-facing runforward/rollback guidance. Success criteria: zero-severity privilege regressions during canaries, <0.1% unauthorized-error delta for canary cohort, automated reconciliation catches >99% of translation mismatches within 24h, and end-to-end audit parity for read/write events. Out of scope: migration UI for self-serve opt-in (handled by PM), persistent schema migration for legacy tokens (separate infra ticket).
steps: 1) Define deterministic policy translation table (v1 permission -> v2 policy assertions) with canonical edge-cases
2) Implement dual-write shim that writes to v1 and v2 with idempotent request IDs and event tagging
3) Wire observability: token-level latency/cost, authorization decision telemetry, and audit event duplication markers
4) Run nightly reconciliation job that computes diff metrics and generates prioritized fix lists
5) Execute staged canaries by org size and permission criticality with synthetic traffic and real-user cohorts
6) Prepare customer rollforward/rollback comms and runbook templates and post-cutover monitoring dashboards
